title: Sulayhid Dynasty
capsule: The Sulayhid dynasty was an Ismaili Shia Arab dynasty in Yemen founded by Ali ibn Muhammad al-Sulayhi, who launched his movement from a stronghold on Jabal Massar around 1047 and conquered all of Yemen by 1062, then extended Fatimid authority northward into the Hejaz, briefly installing his appointees in Mecca and Medina. The dynasty functioned as a Fatimid viceroyalty and brought Yemen administrative cohesion described as unmatched since the Himyarite period. Ali al-Sulayhi was assassinated in 1067 by the Najahid ruler of Zabid; his son al-Mukarram Ahmad recovered much of the territory but power effectively passed to Arwa al-Sulayhi, the only woman to be granted the Friday prayer (khutba) in her name in medieval Islam, who ruled from Jibla until her death in 1138.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Sulayhid core in highland Yemen is attested in Fatimid and Yemeni chronicles, but the precise northern extent of their Hejaz control and fluctuating frontier with rival dynasties is poorly documented geographically.
